name: Brute Force
description: Adversaries may use brute force techniques to systematically guess passwords and gain access to user accounts.

name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
description: Adversaries may attempt to exploit vulnerabilities such as SQL injection or buffer overflows in Internet-facing applications to gain access.

name: Network Service Discovery
description: Adversaries may enumerate network services and open ports to identify remote systems and exploitable listening services.

name: Application Layer Protocol
description: Adversaries may communicate using application layer protocols such as HTTP or HTTPS to blend in with normal network traffic and avoid detection.

name: Command and Scripting Interpreter
description: Adversaries may abuse command and script interpreters such as PowerShell or Unix Shell to execute commands and malicious scripts.

name: Valid Accounts
description: Adversaries may obtain and abuse credentials of existing accounts as a means of gaining initial access and maintaining persistence.

name: User Execution
description: An adversary may rely on user actions, such as opening a malicious email attachment or clicking a link, to gain code execution.

name: Process Injection
description: Adversaries may inject code into processes in order to evade process-based defenses as well as possibly elevate privileges.

name: Remote Services
description: Adversaries may use valid credentials to log into remote services like SSH, RDP, or SMB to move laterally across an internal network.

name: Exfiltration Over C2 Channel
description: Adversaries may exfiltrate stolen data by directing it through their existing command and control communications channel.

name: Network Denial of Service
description: Adversaries may degrade or block the availability of targeted resources to users by exhausting network bandwidth and system resources.

name: File and Directory Discovery
description: Adversaries may enumerate files and directories or search in specific locations to locate sensitive data and configuration files.

name: Phishing
description: Adversaries may send spearphishing emails with malicious attachments or links to compromise target victim workstations.

name: Exploitation for Privilege Escalation
description: Adversaries may exploit software vulnerabilities in operating systems or installed applications to elevate privileges to root or SYSTEM.

name: Active Scanning
description: Adversaries may execute active reconnaissance scans such as vulnerability or port probes to gather information about targeted networks prior to exploitation.
